Its 86.52 on Terminal-Bench 2.1 also exceeds Qwen3.8-Flash-Next's 83.3, DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731's 82.7, and Claude's 78.2. On AA-LCR, Edge0-145B scores 79.3 to Claude's 78.0. These comparisons apply to the named models and evaluations.
Scores are percentages; higher is better. A dash means no public score is available, rather than a score of zero.
Edge0, Qwen, DeepSeek, and Claude results come from Edge0's internal evaluations. Claude-Opus-4.6 has no public DeepSWE 1.1 score. For Flint, Muse Glimmer, and Gemma 4, Terminal-Bench 2.1 and IFBench results come from the Recursive Flint evaluation; HLE, GPQA, and AA-LCR results come from Artificial Analysis.
The largest gains over Qwen3.8-27B, a mainstream on-device model baseline, are in agent and coding work: 18.5% on Terminal-Bench and 53.1% on DeepSWE. The relative gains on HLE, GPQA, and IFBench are 14.9%, 1.3%, and 1.4%, respectively.
DeepSWE 1.1 and Terminal-Bench 2.1 evaluate agent and coding work. HLE, GPQA-Diamond, and IFBench cover reasoning, knowledge, and instruction following. The complete evaluation setup, hardware environment, and reproduction instructions are being released with our technical report.
Competitive capability with a smaller memory footprint
Edge0-145B combines a 72.8 mean score across six benchmarks with 29GB measured peak memory. Qwen3.8-Flash-Next averages 71.7, with an estimated 70GB footprint for standard 4-bit deployment. That puts Edge0-145B at about 40% of the estimated baseline memory while delivering comparable or higher capability, enabling local use on a 48GB laptop.
The means cover DeepSWE 1.1, Terminal-Bench 2.1, HLE, GPQA-Diamond, IFBench, and AA-LCR. Edge0 memory figures are measured internal peaks. Asterisked baseline figures are estimates for standard 4-bit deployment and remain to be measured. Claude is excluded because it is cloud-only and has no DeepSWE score.
[Figure: Quality versus peak memory, with 48GB laptop and 64GB workstation capacities marked. Lower memory and higher scores are better; the chart's vertical axis does not start at zero.]
Local agents that plan, code, run, and check their work
A single natural-language request can start an entire local workflow. Edge0-145B breaks down the requirements, plans the steps, writes code, and calls tools to run it. When something fails, it debugs and repairs the code. It then takes screenshots to inspect the result and keeps iterating until the work is complete.
These projects often take dozens of rounds of planning, execution, and review. Local inference means those additional conversations, code revisions, and visual analyses incur no corresponding cloud-model token or API charges. Code and data can stay on the computer, and core model capabilities work offline.
Video production: generating Tesla's Roadster explainer within an hour
Edge0-145B produced an explainer about how Roadster could fly, handling technical research, scriptwriting, asset generation, and editing. We asked it to make the principles understandable to a general audience. The model ran locally without cloud-model calls or cloud token consumption, avoiding network round trips for inference.
The video was generated within an hour. Producing comparable work manually would have taken a director and scriptwriter, a 3D modeler, an editor, and a physics expert a month. An AI video workflow could previously cost more than hundreds of dollars; local inference eliminates the corresponding cloud-model token and API fees.
3D modeling: a Manhattan city scene in Blender
Edge0-145B built a 3D scene of Manhattan within an hour. Working in Blender from text and reference images, it constructed the scene, adjusted materials and lighting, and iterated on the rendered output.
The workflow brings visual inspection, code generation, and revision together inside Blender. The model works with objects, spatial relationships, and the creative goal, going beyond the pixels in a reference image. It inspects the result, writes code, and makes changes without handing those steps back to a person. The entire process stays local.
Creating a Manhattan-scale city scene manually would typically cost approximately $12,000-18,000 and take at least a month. A leading cloud model would still incur more than $150 in cloud token charges. Edge0-145B completes the local inference without those cloud-model token fees.
Game development: playable games and a medieval city
Edge0-145B can create playable games locally. We also used its 3D modeling capabilities to build an original medieval capital for a fantasy RPG and render a 20-second fly-through at game-trailer quality.
The model planned the city independently and built it from scratch in Blender: city walls, more than a thousand old-town homes, a plaza fountain, a Gothic twin-tower facade, a rib-vaulted nave, and stained-glass windows.
The fixed camera path made errors visible. Geometry clipping, occlusion, or incorrect proportions would appear along the route, so the model inspected the renders and corrected its work as it built. The workflow ran entirely locally.
A leading cloud model required hundreds of tool calls and hundreds of millions of tokens for a single completion, using the same prompt, reference images, and camera route. Edge0-145B delivered it on a laptop without cloud-model token or API fees for local inference. An art team would typically spend weeks and thousands of dollars producing a city scene to this standard.
Hardware control: code that flies a real drone
Edge0-145B wrote the program for a real drone from one instruction: “Write a drone program that navigates through obstacles and finds a red backpack.”
It generated the flight-control and visual-recognition programs locally. The drone then took off indoors, navigated through a dense row of obstacle poles, searched autonomously, and located the red backpack beside a wall. The task required no human-written code and no cloud call.
Hardware developers can describe the behavior they want and have the model turn it into a program for a real device, without moving repeatedly between an editor, documentation, and debugging tools.
PCB design: from KiCad layout to an assembly animation
Edge0-145B took a PCB design from component placement through an assembly visualization. We asked it to design a board for itself. It started from scratch in KiCad, placed components, routed a two-layer board, and imported the design into Unreal Engine 5. It then set up cameras and lighting and rendered an animation of PCB fabrication and assembly.
A single computer delivered work that previously required a hardware engineer and a 3D designer to hand tasks back and forth over several days. Schematics and board layouts can stay on the team's own hardware, supporting trade-secret protection and data-handling requirements without uploading the designs to a cloud model.
Why Edge0: A Full Stack for On-Device AI
Useful on-device AI requires model development, inference engineering, and hardware adaptation to work together. Our progress rests on three capabilities: developing complementary models quickly, optimizing the full stack, and carrying lessons from each deployment into the next.
Our September release of Edge0-35B showed what that approach could deliver on a phone. Its launch post passed 1.2 million views on its first day without paid promotion in overseas communities. Researchers and technical experts at OpenAI, NVIDIA, Qualcomm, and other companies shared it, and the model reached No. 1 on Hugging Face's overall Trending chart.
We released the model weights and unified inference framework together, giving companies and researchers a standard approach they could reproduce. The release helped move the discussion of on-device AI from a few billion parameters to the 35B tier.
Four Model Families for On-Device AI
Over the past year, we released 200 models across four families. Each handles a different part of the work, from listening and speaking to fast decisions, memory, and complex agent tasks.
The portfolio spans tens of millions to more than a hundred billion parameters. Both Edge0 and Audio8 have reached No. 1 on Hugging Face's Trending chart.
Models and Inference Systems Designed Together
We develop the model and the inference framework together, building hardware constraints into training and optimizing the engine for different chips. This connects model capability with the software and hardware needed to use it locally.
That work requires expertise in model development, inference frameworks, and low-level hardware adaptation. The combination is difficult for a company focused only on model development to reproduce.
Hardware Optimizations That Carry into Each Deployment
Each deployment gives us reusable optimizations for the next chip, model, or product. This matters because on-device hardware is fragmented: NPU architectures differ, as does support for numerical formats such as INT4, INT8, and FP4. A general-purpose model cannot automatically make full use of every chip.
We adapt to individual platforms. Our portfolio now covers 95% of mainstream chip platforms, including Qualcomm, BES, Rockchip, Allwinner, D-Robotics, and NVIDIA, across headphones, glasses, phones, PCs, and robots. This is portfolio-wide coverage; model requirements vary, and it does not mean every device can run Edge0-145B.
That deployment work now spans more than 5 million production devices. Our open-source models passed 15 million downloads within three months. By October 2026, we had more than 110,000 customer organizations.
The portfolio figures come from company papers and internal testing. They describe the broader Edge0 portfolio; the 145B performance results in this article apply specifically to Edge0-145B.
For Edge0-145B, day-one support covers macOS, Windows, and Linux, including Apple M-series chips and NVIDIA platforms such as RTX Spark, RTX 4090, and RTX 5090. The release includes one-click deployment tools and hardware guides.
The Future of On-Device AI and the Cloud
More complex work can stay on the device as local models approach cloud-level capability. Privacy, cost control, and offline access have long favored local execution; the remaining question was whether an on-device model could do the work. Edge0-145B expands the range of tasks for which it can.
Why More AI Work Can Stay Local
Local execution addresses four practical obstacles to adopting cloud-only AI:
- Control cloud-model costs. Local inference adds no corresponding cloud-model token or API fees as usage grows.
- Keep sensitive data local. Code, documents, and business records can stay on the hardware, giving teams control over data handling.
- Sustain a responsive experience. Model and inference-engine design address response speed, power use, system responsiveness, and continuous operation together.
- Keep core capabilities available offline. Local tasks continue when connectivity drops; features that depend on online information or services still need a connection.
From Cloud First to More Complex Work On-Device
We see the division of work between devices and the cloud shifting through three stages.
Before September 2026: cloud first, with on-device support. Apple Intelligence reflected this stage: it protected privacy, but handled a limited range of tasks locally while more demanding work relied on cloud capabilities.
After Edge0-35B's September 10 release: everyday tasks locally, complex tasks in the cloud. Local models could take on frequent requests that needed immediate responses. For one leading headphone manufacturer, our hybrid solution now handles 92% of AI usage on-device and 8% in the cloud. Everyday conversation accounts for most use cases on consumer wearables.
With Edge0-145B: toward on-device first, with cloud support. Vibe coding and other complex tasks can now run on a personal computer, giving teams more scope to choose local execution. This extends the range of work that can stay on the device while preserving the cloud for tasks and hardware that need it.
The diagram shows the shift from cloud-first AI to everyday local tasks and then more complex local work. Its colored areas are schematic, not measured usage shares.
Where Cloud AI Still Fits
Hardware constraints still determine which model fits. Compute capacity, heat, and battery life matter: Edge0-35B runs on phones, while Edge0-145B runs on suitably equipped laptops. A very low-compute device cannot currently run a 145B model locally. It needs a smaller model suited to its hardware or cloud access to a model of that size.
Cross-device long-term memory and searches requiring highly current information still require cloud services. Local and cloud models can work together; the appropriate split depends on the task, the hardware, and the information it needs.
The aim is to make local execution a practical choice for demanding work, with a capable model that can keep working close to the person using it. That is the next step toward our goal of enabling intelligence at zero distance for everybody.
Get Started with Edge0
Download the models to run locally, evaluate or fine-tune them, and build them into your own products:
- Model weights: Edge0-145B and Edge0-120B on Hugging Face.
- Inference framework and deployment guides: Edge0 on GitHub.
- Try it without environment setup: Download the Edge0 App. Its core model capabilities work offline, without an account or usage quota.
- Community: Join us on Discord.
For hardware or product integrations, reach the Edge0 team through GitHub or contact@autoark.ai.

articles.title: Global Microsoft Outage
articles.body:
Our live coverage has ended
Read more about the Microsoft outage here or scroll through the posts below to learn more.
Updates
(29)
Where things stand with the disruptive Microsoft service outage
• Coming back online: Microsoft said it has addressed the underlying issue of a massive outage that affected millions around the world as it continues to restore service. The software giant apologized for disruptions, saying the outage was caused by a technical issue and not a cybersecurity breach.
• Economic ramifications: The cost of lost productivity from the outage could approach at least $7 billion, according to a think-tank estimate.
• What’s been impacted: The outage, which began around noon ET on Thursday, left workers unable to access Outlook email, Teams meeting tools and other staples of modern office life. AI companies said they were facing issues as well. Banks, governments, health services, railways and courts all reported disruptions across Microsoft products.
• Global disruption: Outage reports “reached 74 countries and territories in about an hour,” according to Downdetector. While some workers scrambled to find workarounds, others expressed relief in a respite from the work grind.
US city governments say services are returning after outage
US cities are beginning to report Microsoft services returning after a widespread outage that began yesterday hit governments across the country and world.
Jacksonville, Florida, said that it was “seeing some services restored this morning and remain cautiously optimistic they will continue making progress.”
Austin and Dallas also reported progress on their email services being restored. The sheriff’s office in Arapahoe County, Colorado, which had previously reported the outage affecting online bond payments, said the issue was resolved.
Microsoft said this morning that the “underlying issue” that caused the massive outage had been addressed and that it was seeing recovery across its services.
The police department of Greensboro, North Carolina, also saw its services being restored. “While it’s not the outcome we wanted, we would like to let you know that our email is working again,” the department jested.
Microsoft services returning to normal after hours of disruption. Catch up on the latest
After hours of disruption affecting millions of users worldwide, Outlook and other Microsoft services are finally returning to normal.
Microsoft has apologized for the outage, which could end up costing billions in lost productivity.
The company reported “encouraging recovery progress” saying that queues of emails waiting to be delivered are “significantly reduced and approaching normal levels.”
Here’s what to know:
What was disrupted? Any of the applications involving email or Microsoft’s Exchange Online Services were affected, the company said. That left users likely unable to access or send new emails, use Microsoft’s AI tool Copilot, or join pre-scheduled Teams meetings already in the calendar. Other services — like those that share documents, pool a company’s data or protect emails — might also have been affected.
What’s the impact? The outage left millions without the work tools they use every day and could cost $7 billion in lost productivity, according to an estimate by a Michigan think tank. Patrick Anderson, Anderson Economic Group’s president, said that perhaps as many as 26 million users on Thursday and 51 million users on Friday have actually seen their operations disrupted in a way that caused an economic loss. And he said the cost will likely increase beyond this initial estimate.
City governments across the US reported disruption, encouraging residents to call local offices if necessary. Some Brits experienced delays in getting their drug prescriptions and several UK police forces told the public to report crimes or issues by telephone rather than through their websites.
Meanwhile, bank workers in Hong Kong had their work disrupted, government employees in Japan resorted to creating physical copies of documents and courts in the Philippines were hindered by the outage. Some railway networks experienced disruption to their customer email services and routing schedules while Australian schools, courts and government services reported disruption.
What caused this? Microsoft said the outage was caused by a “technical issue” rather than any cybersecurity breach. “The incident was introduced by an issue during an earlier network capacity upgrade that surfaced following a recent network change,” the company said.
CNN’s Gage Goulding, Anna Cooban, August Phillips, Hanna Ziady, Karina Tsui, Helen Regan, Kathleen Magramo and Chris Isidore contributed reporting
Microsoft apologizes, says underlying cause of outage has been addressed
Microsoft has addressed the “underlying issue” that caused a massive outage affecting millions across the world, the tech company said, adding that it was “seeing broad recovery and stability across our services.”
Microsoft offered some explanation of what caused the outage that began yesterday, confirming it was a “technical issue” and not a cybersecurity or AI-related concern.
“The incident was introduced by an issue during an earlier network capacity upgrade that surfaced following a recent network change,” Microsoft said.
The software giant said it would release a “full post-incident report” after a review.
Cost of Microsoft outage could top $7 billion, according to estimate
The cost of lost productivity from the Microsoft outage could approach $7 billion, according to an estimate by a Michigan think tank on Friday.
Anderson Economic Group, which is known for cautious estimates on the costs of economic disruptions, including labor strikes and tariffs, said that many of the reported 430 million Microsoft users who have been affected likely only are dealing with annoyances, rather than true lost productivity.
But Patrick Anderson, the firm’s president, said that perhaps as many as 26 million users on Thursday and 51 million users on Friday have actually seen their operations disrupted in a way that caused an economic loss. And he said the cost will likely increase beyond this initial estimate.
“This is a starting point, with all the limitations on what we know. We don’t know complete scale,” he told CNN on Friday.
Some companies might be able to be compensated by cybersecurity insurance policies for the costs associated with the outage – but that would only shift the cost from the Microsoft users to their insurers.
In addition, Anderson estimated that Microsoft could conceivably need to refund customers about $800 million a day in subscription fees for services they pay for under contracts but could not access. While not all customers will seek refunds, those who do so are likely to push the total cost of the outage above $7 billion, Anderson said.
The outage, which began around noon ET on Thursday, left workers unable to access Outlook email, Teams meeting tools and other staples of modern office life, as well as the company’s Copilot AI chatbot.
Emails are "approaching normal levels” after outage, Microsoft says
Outlook is returning to normal after hours of disruption, as queues of email waiting to be delivered are “significantly reduced and approaching normal levels,” Microsoft said.
The company is continuing to observe “improvements in service availability,” it said in a statement this morning. “Some users may still experience intermittent access issues or delayed email delivery as recovery continues,” it added.
Microsoft seeing "broader improvements" in North America
Microsoft just said it is seeing “encouraging recovery progress” at the same time as some social media users and CNN journalists report receiving emails in their inboxes again.
In a statement on X, the company reported “email delivery performance improving across a growing portion of affected Microsoft 365 infrastructure,” but warned some users may still “experience intermittent issues.”
While some social media users reported getting emails again, others said they were still unable to access them.
In an additional update issued later, Microsoft outlined the uneven pace of recovery in different regions. The company indicated that North America was recovering faster than Europe and Asia.
It reported “broader improvements in North America, sustained improvements across much of Europe, and encouraging recovery signals in Asia Pacific.”
UK police forces urge public to report crimes via telephone, not online
Several UK police forces told the public Friday to report crimes or issues by telephone rather than through their websites amid the Microsoft outage.
Police forces in Merseyside, Greater Manchester and Bedfordshire informed visitors to their websites that online submission forms were disrupted.
East Hertfordshire Police said in a statement posted to X that “some online form submissions on our website may be affected” because of the outage.
In another Friday post on X, Dorset Police said it was “unable to receive online form submissions.”
All police forces urged the public to call 101 if their issue is “time-critical but not an emergency.” (The UK emergency number is 999).
Microsoft says services are being "gradually restored"
Microsoft says it is making “additional progress toward recovery” and that traffic is “being gradually restored” as its engineers scramble to fix the worldwide outage that has left millions without the work tools they use every day.
In a statement, Microsoft said it is “seeing improvements in key scenarios, including mailbox access and delayed email processing, though some intermittent issues may continue.”
What to know as you're waking up in the US without email
Outlook is still down, as Microsoft’s rolling outage – now extending into a second day – continues to affect services for millions of people around the world.
The outage, which is also affecting Teams and Copilot, is disrupting government and business operations in the United States and elsewhere, with at least one company postponing a quarterly earnings call.
Microsoft executive Charles Lamanna said in the early hours of Friday that there is currently no indication that the outage is the result “of malicious or cyber activity.”
Here’s what to know:
Email down: Outlook remains down and users are also having trouble accessing their Exchange Online mailboxes.
In an update at around 4:15 a.m. ET Friday, Microsoft said it would extend its “email timeout window” to 48 hours “to help protect delayed messages while service recovery continues.”
The email timeout window is the maximum amount of time that a mail server or email client such as Outlook will spend waiting to receive an email before returning an error.
AI companies affected: OpenAI said it was facing issues with Microsoft connectors, with some tools, including ChatGPT, not working “as expected.” Meanwhile, thousands of Claude AI users reported issues Friday morning, according to Downdetector. Claude creator Anthropic said shortly after 6 a.m. ET that a fix had been deployed and it was “monitoring for recovery.”
US lawmakers: The US House of Representatives said the outage impacted its users and its engineers were working with Microsoft, according to Reuters. Some congressional staffers expressed frustration on X. “Shall we start conducting all official business via DM?” said Sharon Eliza Nichols, communications director for Congresswoman Eleanor Holmes Norton.
US cities: City governments across the United States have reported email disruptions and have encouraged residents to call local offices and agencies if necessary.
- Several police and sheriff departments said the outage was affecting their email and communication platforms, including Colorado’s Arapahoe Sheriff’s Office, which said the outage had delayed the processing of prisoners’ bail payments.
- The outages are affecting email services in Miami Beach, Austin, and Jacksonville, though officials assured residents that emergency services were still active.
- In California, officials from Pasadena, Fremont, Burbank, and Santa Barbara also issued statements warning of downed email use.
- Baltimore County officials said on X that government staff could not send or receive emails and urged residents to contact relevant departments by phone.
Earnings call delayed: Workhorse Group, a Detroit-based electric vehicle manufacturer, pushed its third quarter earnings call to Monday, citing “business disruptions caused by the global Microsoft outages.”
CNN’s Gage Goulding contributed reporting.
What is affected by the outage?
Some office workers rely on Microsoft’s suite of applications for practically everything – emails, meetings, AI, creating spreadsheets, and writing and sharing documents. Any of those functions which involve email or Microsoft’s Exchange Online services are impacted, the company said.
Outlook: Email is the main thing impacted by the outage, leaving users likely unable to access or send any new emails.
Copilot: Users may also be unable to load chats with or receive responses from Microsoft’s AI tool. Copilot also cannot access the data it normally draws from, like emails, files and calendars.
Teams: Anything that has already been scheduled and requires Teams — Microsoft’s communications platform — to connect with a user’s calendar is likely impacted. But if users are simply just joining a call or exchanging messages, that is still working.
Word/Excel/Powerpoint: The basic functions of these apps are still working. However, other functions may be impacted, like if users are trying to print documents over the cloud or share documents with Sharepoint. Users may also not be able to view their most recently used files.
Other, more specialist Microsoft services – like those which pool a company’s data or allow IT to monitor a company’s devices – may also be affected.
It's a disappointing day for some workers using Gmail
While many workers using Microsoft’s systems have spent Friday rejoicing that they’re forced to take a break — unable to send or receive emails or conduct their usual Teams calls — those using Google services are lamenting in memes shared on social media.
Google systems including Gmail, Google Docs and Google Meet appear to be functioning just fine, or at least well enough to promise users an average working Friday.
One video on Instagram shows someone lying in bed with the word “Outlook” above their head. Another sits at a desk working on their laptop with the word “Gmail” above theirs.
Another video shows a meme of actor Pedro Pascal appearing to sob uncontrollably under text reading: “When you hear Outlook is down and start planning your afternoon wines… Then remember your workplace uses Google Workspace.”
Railways report communications delay due to Microsoft service disruption
Some railway networks are experiencing disruptions to their customer email services and routing schedules because of the Microsoft outage.
VIA Rail Canada said passengers “may not be able to receive email communications about their trip” due to technical issues with Microsoft services. The railway asked passengers to check their web-based train tracker or subscribe to SMS notifications for information on their journeys.
Germany’s Deutsche Bahn said Microsoft Outlook is experiencing “severe sluggishness,” causing significant delays in its abilities to send out and receive emails.
“As a result, the distribution of rerouting schedules is severely restricted. All relevant teams are involved in resolving the issue; current indications point to a server-side problem on Microsoft’s end,” it said in a statement.
In the UK, National Rail, which runs passenger rail services in England, Scotland and Wales, said the ongoing outage may be affecting customers’ ability to access train tickets by email.
It advised travelers to visit the website or app where tickets were purchased, or to contact the ticket retailer directly.
“If you are still unable to access your ticket, please contact a member of onboard staff or station staff for advice,” National Rail said on its website.
Rail Delivery Group, which manages National Rail, said there were no current disruptions to operations or train services as a result of the outage.
CNN’s Nina Avramova contributed to this report.
Microsoft extends email timeout window to 48 hours amid outage
Microsoft said that it would extend its email timeout window to 48 hours “to help protect delayed messages while service recovery continues,” according to an update posted at around 4:15 a.m. ET Friday.
The email timeout window is the maximum amount of time that a mail server or email client such as Outlook will spend waiting to receive an email before returning an error.
Microsoft said recovery efforts are ongoing and that it’s seeing “early signs of stabilization,” though service capacity has not returned to normal.
It's Friday and Microsoft is still down. (Some) workers are taking it easy
Memes and jokes abounded online as the global outage of Microsoft’s Outlook emails and Teams meeting platform crossed the 12-hour mark.
One joke that spread on Threads, X and LinkedIn was the rebrand of Microsoft365 to Microsoft364 – memorializing the one day of the year that the software company went dark.
Others reveled at not needing to respond to constant emails and notifications for at least one day.
Another account wrote: “Outlook is down. Your email does not find me well. It does not find me at all.”
Others on Reddit said they panicked and thought they were laid off when they could not access their work emails.
Here's where we're seeing the outage's impacts
At first, Microsoft said the connection issues were happening “in the Americas,” but over time it became clear the troubles were global.
Microsoft’s outage reports “reached 74 countries and territories in about an hour,” according to Downdetector, a website that tracks cyber outages.
Here’s where we’ve seen reports of outages:
- Australian schools, courts and government services started their Friday morning with Microsoft Outlook and other apps out of service.
- In Hong Kong, workers from banks including Morgan Stanley and Goldman Sachs told CNN their work was disrupted, as they were unable to access emails or Teams from the moment they signed on and all through their lunch break. “Sporadically some mails come in but there is probably millions of backlog to process,” one banker told CNN before heading off for lunch break.
- The disruption has also hit Japan’s government services, Deputy Chief Cabinet Secretary Masanao Ozaki said in a Friday presser. Government employees are responding to the outage by creating physical copies of documents, he added. Government ministries and agencies have been unable to send emails through most of the Friday workday.
- Courts in the Philippines are also being slowed down by the Microsoft disruption, the Supreme Court said. “During this period, responses to emails and other transactions may be delayed,” it added in a post on X.
- In the UK, a disruption to the National Health Service email system is expected to prevent some patients from getting their drug prescriptions.
CNN’s Brian Stelter, Hilary Whiteman and Junko Ogura contributed to this report.
Britons can expect delays in accessing prescribed medication today, says UK pharmacy group
A Microsoft outage causing disruptions to the email system of the UK’s National Health Service is expected to prevent some patients from getting their drug prescriptions Friday.
The outage “affects a pharmacy’s ability to communicate with GP practices and some patients,” a spokesperson for the National Pharmacy Association said in a Friday statement.
GPs are equivalent to family doctors in the US.
An NPA spokesperson told CNN in a separate phone call that, while many patients will get their medications, those with more complex prescriptions requiring a pharmacist to contact the prescribing doctor to check or query any details could experience delays.
The spokesperson added that Fridays are typically busy days at pharmacies.
“It’s just a massive pain. It will be slow today,” they said.
Microsoft reports "marginal success" in patching servers
More than 12 hours after Microsoft first warned of a global outage affecting some of its most popular products, the company said it had “observed marginal success” in fixing the problem.
“We’re continuing to monitor activity across regions to evaluate server status and determine actions that can be taken to improve capacity,” Microsoft said in a statement posted on its Service Health Status page early Friday.
“At this point, we have observed marginal success,” the company wrote.
Around 30 minutes later, Microsoft posted another statement saying the company has seen “positive results for service stability and increased capacity as a result of our latest traffic optimization actions.”
Reiterating what it said earlier Thursday, Microsoft stated it was not aware of any malicious activity causing the outage but will continue to treat the incident “with urgency and priority until full resolution.”
More than 12 hours into Microsoft's outage, here's what to know
The Microsoft global outage is ongoing after the US tech giant first reported problems with its email services on Thursday.
More than 430 million people use Microsoft 365 apps and more than 90% of Fortune 500 companies use its Copilot AI chatbot, according to the company’s website.
Millions worldwide lost access to Outlook email, Teams meeting tools and other essentials of modern office life as the disruption quickly spread.
The company reported “marginal success” in repairing the outage in its latest update, early Friday ET. A Microsoft executive confirmed the outage was not the result of a security breach.
As Europe woke on Friday, the outage remained widespread.
Here’s the latest if you’re just tuning in:
- Return to sender: The outage hit in 74 countries and territories in around an hour, according to tracking website Downdetector. Several airlines reported disruptions to their email support.
- In the US: City governments countrywide reported widespread email disruptions and encouraged residents to call local offices and agencies if necessary. At least one American company postponed its quarterly earnings call.
- In Asia Pacific: Some of Japan’s government services switched to paper documents due to the outage and courts in the Philippines experienced delays. Australian schools, courts and government services were also affected. In Hong Kong, staff at Morgan Stanley and Goldman Sachs told CNN their work was disrupted through to their lunch break.
- Scams warning: Banks warned customers to beware of scams and phishing attempts as cybercriminals may use the outage to target individuals and businesses.
CNN’s Helen Regan, Hilary Whiteman, Karina Tsui, Kathleen Magramo and Ross Adkin contributed reporting.
Some airlines report comms disruptions due to Microsoft outage
Several airlines are reporting disruptions to their email support and communications due to the Microsoft outage, posting statements to customers on social media.
Indian budget carrier IndiGo said its “email support services are currently impacted, and we may not be able to receive your emails.” It directed customers to reach out via their website or mobile app.
Akasa Air, another low-cost Indian carrier, similarly said its “email support services are currently experiencing delays.”
And South African carrier CemAir said it was “experiencing some system disruptions due to the global Microsoft outage.”
None of the carriers reported flight disruptions.
Indian flag carrier Air India said it was “closely monitoring the ongoing Microsoft outage” and has rerouted emails. The airline said its flight operations “remain unaffected” and “there is currently no impact on any of our communication channels.”
“Consider this your cue to plan that getaway.”

articles.title: Global Microsoft Outage
articles.body:
Our live coverage has ended
Read more about the Microsoft outage here or scroll through the posts below to learn more.
Updates
(29)
Where things stand with the disruptive Microsoft service outage
• Coming back online: Microsoft said it has addressed the underlying issue of a massive outage that affected millions around the world as it continues to restore service. The software giant apologized for disruptions, saying the outage was caused by a technical issue and not a cybersecurity breach.
• Economic ramifications: The cost of lost productivity from the outage could approach at least $7 billion, according to a think-tank estimate.
• What’s been impacted: The outage, which began around noon ET on Thursday, left workers unable to access Outlook email, Teams meeting tools and other staples of modern office life. AI companies said they were facing issues as well. Banks, governments, health services, railways and courts all reported disruptions across Microsoft products.
• Global disruption: Outage reports “reached 74 countries and territories in about an hour,” according to Downdetector. While some workers scrambled to find workarounds, others expressed relief in a respite from the work grind.
US city governments say services are returning after outage
US cities are beginning to report Microsoft services returning after a widespread outage that began yesterday hit governments across the country and world.
Jacksonville, Florida, said that it was “seeing some services restored this morning and remain cautiously optimistic they will continue making progress.”
Austin and Dallas also reported progress on their email services being restored. The sheriff’s office in Arapahoe County, Colorado, which had previously reported the outage affecting online bond payments, said the issue was resolved.
Microsoft said this morning that the “underlying issue” that caused the massive outage had been addressed and that it was seeing recovery across its services.
The police department of Greensboro, North Carolina, also saw its services being restored. “While it’s not the outcome we wanted, we would like to let you know that our email is working again,” the department jested.
Microsoft services returning to normal after hours of disruption. Catch up on the latest
After hours of disruption affecting millions of users worldwide, Outlook and other Microsoft services are finally returning to normal.
Microsoft has apologized for the outage, which could end up costing billions in lost productivity.
The company reported “encouraging recovery progress” saying that queues of emails waiting to be delivered are “significantly reduced and approaching normal levels.”
Here’s what to know:
What was disrupted? Any of the applications involving email or Microsoft’s Exchange Online Services were affected, the company said. That left users likely unable to access or send new emails, use Microsoft’s AI tool Copilot, or join pre-scheduled Teams meetings already in the calendar. Other services — like those that share documents, pool a company’s data or protect emails — might also have been affected.
What’s the impact? The outage left millions without the work tools they use every day and could cost $7 billion in lost productivity, according to an estimate by a Michigan think tank. Patrick Anderson, Anderson Economic Group’s president, said that perhaps as many as 26 million users on Thursday and 51 million users on Friday have actually seen their operations disrupted in a way that caused an economic loss. And he said the cost will likely increase beyond this initial estimate.
City governments across the US reported disruption, encouraging residents to call local offices if necessary. Some Brits experienced delays in getting their drug prescriptions and several UK police forces told the public to report crimes or issues by telephone rather than through their websites.
Meanwhile, bank workers in Hong Kong had their work disrupted, government employees in Japan resorted to creating physical copies of documents and courts in the Philippines were hindered by the outage. Some railway networks experienced disruption to their customer email services and routing schedules while Australian schools, courts and government services reported disruption.
What caused this? Microsoft said the outage was caused by a “technical issue” rather than any cybersecurity breach. “The incident was introduced by an issue during an earlier network capacity upgrade that surfaced following a recent network change,” the company said.
CNN’s Gage Goulding, Anna Cooban, August Phillips, Hanna Ziady, Karina Tsui, Helen Regan, Kathleen Magramo and Chris Isidore contributed reporting
Microsoft apologizes, says underlying cause of outage has been addressed
Microsoft has addressed the “underlying issue” that caused a massive outage affecting millions across the world, the tech company said, adding that it was “seeing broad recovery and stability across our services.”
Microsoft offered some explanation of what caused the outage that began yesterday, confirming it was a “technical issue” and not a cybersecurity or AI-related concern.
“The incident was introduced by an issue during an earlier network capacity upgrade that surfaced following a recent network change,” Microsoft said.
The software giant said it would release a “full post-incident report” after a review.
Cost of Microsoft outage could top $7 billion, according to estimate
The cost of lost productivity from the Microsoft outage could approach $7 billion, according to an estimate by a Michigan think tank on Friday.
Anderson Economic Group, which is known for cautious estimates on the costs of economic disruptions, including labor strikes and tariffs, said that many of the reported 430 million Microsoft users who have been affected likely only are dealing with annoyances, rather than true lost productivity.
But Patrick Anderson, the firm’s president, said that perhaps as many as 26 million users on Thursday and 51 million users on Friday have actually seen their operations disrupted in a way that caused an economic loss. And he said the cost will likely increase beyond this initial estimate.
“This is a starting point, with all the limitations on what we know. We don’t know complete scale,” he told CNN on Friday.
Some companies might be able to be compensated by cybersecurity insurance policies for the costs associated with the outage – but that would only shift the cost from the Microsoft users to their insurers.
In addition, Anderson estimated that Microsoft could conceivably need to refund customers about $800 million a day in subscription fees for services they pay for under contracts but could not access. While not all customers will seek refunds, those who do so are likely to push the total cost of the outage above $7 billion, Anderson said.
The outage, which began around noon ET on Thursday, left workers unable to access Outlook email, Teams meeting tools and other staples of modern office life, as well as the company’s Copilot AI chatbot.
Emails are "approaching normal levels” after outage, Microsoft says
Outlook is returning to normal after hours of disruption, as queues of email waiting to be delivered are “significantly reduced and approaching normal levels,” Microsoft said.
The company is continuing to observe “improvements in service availability,” it said in a statement this morning. “Some users may still experience intermittent access issues or delayed email delivery as recovery continues,” it added.
Microsoft seeing "broader improvements" in North America
Microsoft just said it is seeing “encouraging recovery progress” at the same time as some social media users and CNN journalists report receiving emails in their inboxes again.
In a statement on X, the company reported “email delivery performance improving across a growing portion of affected Microsoft 365 infrastructure,” but warned some users may still “experience intermittent issues.”
While some social media users reported getting emails again, others said they were still unable to access them.
In an additional update issued later, Microsoft outlined the uneven pace of recovery in different regions. The company indicated that North America was recovering faster than Europe and Asia.
It reported “broader improvements in North America, sustained improvements across much of Europe, and encouraging recovery signals in Asia Pacific.”
UK police forces urge public to report crimes via telephone, not online
Several UK police forces told the public Friday to report crimes or issues by telephone rather than through their websites amid the Microsoft outage.
Police forces in Merseyside, Greater Manchester and Bedfordshire informed visitors to their websites that online submission forms were disrupted.
East Hertfordshire Police said in a statement posted to X that “some online form submissions on our website may be affected” because of the outage.
In another Friday post on X, Dorset Police said it was “unable to receive online form submissions.”
All police forces urged the public to call 101 if their issue is “time-critical but not an emergency.” (The UK emergency number is 999).
Microsoft says services are being "gradually restored"
Microsoft says it is making “additional progress toward recovery” and that traffic is “being gradually restored” as its engineers scramble to fix the worldwide outage that has left millions without the work tools they use every day.
In a statement, Microsoft said it is “seeing improvements in key scenarios, including mailbox access and delayed email processing, though some intermittent issues may continue.”
What to know as you're waking up in the US without email
Outlook is still down, as Microsoft’s rolling outage – now extending into a second day – continues to affect services for millions of people around the world.
The outage, which is also affecting Teams and Copilot, is disrupting government and business operations in the United States and elsewhere, with at least one company postponing a quarterly earnings call.
Microsoft executive Charles Lamanna said in the early hours of Friday that there is currently no indication that the outage is the result “of malicious or cyber activity.”
Here’s what to know:
Email down: Outlook remains down and users are also having trouble accessing their Exchange Online mailboxes.
In an update at around 4:15 a.m. ET Friday, Microsoft said it would extend its “email timeout window” to 48 hours “to help protect delayed messages while service recovery continues.”
The email timeout window is the maximum amount of time that a mail server or email client such as Outlook will spend waiting to receive an email before returning an error.
AI companies affected: OpenAI said it was facing issues with Microsoft connectors, with some tools, including ChatGPT, not working “as expected.” Meanwhile, thousands of Claude AI users reported issues Friday morning, according to Downdetector. Claude creator Anthropic said shortly after 6 a.m. ET that a fix had been deployed and it was “monitoring for recovery.”
US lawmakers: The US House of Representatives said the outage impacted its users and its engineers were working with Microsoft, according to Reuters. Some congressional staffers expressed frustration on X. “Shall we start conducting all official business via DM?” said Sharon Eliza Nichols, communications director for Congresswoman Eleanor Holmes Norton.
US cities: City governments across the United States have reported email disruptions and have encouraged residents to call local offices and agencies if necessary.
- Several police and sheriff departments said the outage was affecting their email and communication platforms, including Colorado’s Arapahoe Sheriff’s Office, which said the outage had delayed the processing of prisoners’ bail payments.
- The outages are affecting email services in Miami Beach, Austin, and Jacksonville, though officials assured residents that emergency services were still active.
- In California, officials from Pasadena, Fremont, Burbank, and Santa Barbara also issued statements warning of downed email use.
- Baltimore County officials said on X that government staff could not send or receive emails and urged residents to contact relevant departments by phone.
Earnings call delayed: Workhorse Group, a Detroit-based electric vehicle manufacturer, pushed its third quarter earnings call to Monday, citing “business disruptions caused by the global Microsoft outages.”
CNN’s Gage Goulding contributed reporting.
What is affected by the outage?
Some office workers rely on Microsoft’s suite of applications for practically everything – emails, meetings, AI, creating spreadsheets, and writing and sharing documents. Any of those functions which involve email or Microsoft’s Exchange Online services are impacted, the company said.
Outlook: Email is the main thing impacted by the outage, leaving users likely unable to access or send any new emails.
Copilot: Users may also be unable to load chats with or receive responses from Microsoft’s AI tool. Copilot also cannot access the data it normally draws from, like emails, files and calendars.
Teams: Anything that has already been scheduled and requires Teams — Microsoft’s communications platform — to connect with a user’s calendar is likely impacted. But if users are simply just joining a call or exchanging messages, that is still working.
Word/Excel/Powerpoint: The basic functions of these apps are still working. However, other functions may be impacted, like if users are trying to print documents over the cloud or share documents with Sharepoint. Users may also not be able to view their most recently used files.
Other, more specialist Microsoft services – like those which pool a company’s data or allow IT to monitor a company’s devices – may also be affected.
It's a disappointing day for some workers using Gmail
While many workers using Microsoft’s systems have spent Friday rejoicing that they’re forced to take a break — unable to send or receive emails or conduct their usual Teams calls — those using Google services are lamenting in memes shared on social media.
Google systems including Gmail, Google Docs and Google Meet appear to be functioning just fine, or at least well enough to promise users an average working Friday.
One video on Instagram shows someone lying in bed with the word “Outlook” above their head. Another sits at a desk working on their laptop with the word “Gmail” above theirs.
Another video shows a meme of actor Pedro Pascal appearing to sob uncontrollably under text reading: “When you hear Outlook is down and start planning your afternoon wines… Then remember your workplace uses Google Workspace.”
Railways report communications delay due to Microsoft service disruption
Some railway networks are experiencing disruptions to their customer email services and routing schedules because of the Microsoft outage.
VIA Rail Canada said passengers “may not be able to receive email communications about their trip” due to technical issues with Microsoft services. The railway asked passengers to check their web-based train tracker or subscribe to SMS notifications for information on their journeys.
Germany’s Deutsche Bahn said Microsoft Outlook is experiencing “severe sluggishness,” causing significant delays in its abilities to send out and receive emails.
“As a result, the distribution of rerouting schedules is severely restricted. All relevant teams are involved in resolving the issue; current indications point to a server-side problem on Microsoft’s end,” it said in a statement.
In the UK, National Rail, which runs passenger rail services in England, Scotland and Wales, said the ongoing outage may be affecting customers’ ability to access train tickets by email.
It advised travelers to visit the website or app where tickets were purchased, or to contact the ticket retailer directly.
“If you are still unable to access your ticket, please contact a member of onboard staff or station staff for advice,” National Rail said on its website.
Rail Delivery Group, which manages National Rail, said there were no current disruptions to operations or train services as a result of the outage.
CNN’s Nina Avramova contributed to this report.
Microsoft extends email timeout window to 48 hours amid outage
Microsoft said that it would extend its email timeout window to 48 hours “to help protect delayed messages while service recovery continues,” according to an update posted at around 4:15 a.m. ET Friday.
The email timeout window is the maximum amount of time that a mail server or email client such as Outlook will spend waiting to receive an email before returning an error.
Microsoft said recovery efforts are ongoing and that it’s seeing “early signs of stabilization,” though service capacity has not returned to normal.
It's Friday and Microsoft is still down. (Some) workers are taking it easy
Memes and jokes abounded online as the global outage of Microsoft’s Outlook emails and Teams meeting platform crossed the 12-hour mark.
One joke that spread on Threads, X and LinkedIn was the rebrand of Microsoft365 to Microsoft364 – memorializing the one day of the year that the software company went dark.
Others reveled at not needing to respond to constant emails and notifications for at least one day.
Another account wrote: “Outlook is down. Your email does not find me well. It does not find me at all.”
Others on Reddit said they panicked and thought they were laid off when they could not access their work emails.
Here's where we're seeing the outage's impacts
At first, Microsoft said the connection issues were happening “in the Americas,” but over time it became clear the troubles were global.
Microsoft’s outage reports “reached 74 countries and territories in about an hour,” according to Downdetector, a website that tracks cyber outages.
Here’s where we’ve seen reports of outages:

- In Hong Kong, workers from banks including Morgan Stanley and Goldman Sachs told CNN their work was disrupted, as they were unable to access emails or Teams from the moment they signed on and all through their lunch break. “Sporadically some mails come in but there is probably millions of backlog to process,” one banker told CNN before heading off for lunch break.
- The disruption has also hit Japan’s government services, Deputy Chief Cabinet Secretary Masanao Ozaki said in a Friday presser. Government employees are responding to the outage by creating physical copies of documents, he added. Government ministries and agencies have been unable to send emails through most of the Friday workday.
- Courts in the Philippines are also being slowed down by the Microsoft disruption, the Supreme Court said. “During this period, responses to emails and other transactions may be delayed,” it added in a post on X.
- In the UK, a disruption to the National Health Service email system is expected to prevent some patients from getting their drug prescriptions.
CNN’s Brian Stelter, Hilary Whiteman and Junko Ogura contributed to this report.
Britons can expect delays in accessing prescribed medication today, says UK pharmacy group
A Microsoft outage causing disruptions to the email system of the UK’s National Health Service is expected to prevent some patients from getting their drug prescriptions Friday.
The outage “affects a pharmacy’s ability to communicate with GP practices and some patients,” a spokesperson for the National Pharmacy Association said in a Friday statement.
GPs are equivalent to family doctors in the US.
An NPA spokesperson told CNN in a separate phone call that, while many patients will get their medications, those with more complex prescriptions requiring a pharmacist to contact the prescribing doctor to check or query any details could experience delays.
The spokesperson added that Fridays are typically busy days at pharmacies.
“It’s just a massive pain. It will be slow today,” they said.
Microsoft reports "marginal success" in patching servers
More than 12 hours after Microsoft first warned of a global outage affecting some of its most popular products, the company said it had “observed marginal success” in fixing the problem.
“We’re continuing to monitor activity across regions to evaluate server status and determine actions that can be taken to improve capacity,” Microsoft said in a statement posted on its Service Health Status page early Friday.
“At this point, we have observed marginal success,” the company wrote.
Around 30 minutes later, Microsoft posted another statement saying the company has seen “positive results for service stability and increased capacity as a result of our latest traffic optimization actions.”
Reiterating what it said earlier Thursday, Microsoft stated it was not aware of any malicious activity causing the outage but will continue to treat the incident “with urgency and priority until full resolution.”

Akasa Air, another low-cost Indian carrier, similarly said its “email support services are currently experiencing delays.”
And South African carrier CemAir said it was “experiencing some system disruptions due to the global Microsoft outage.”

articles.title: Jensen Huang was reckless with the environment, too
articles.body:
Under cofounder Jensen Huang, Nvidia has become the engine for the AI boom — and one of the tech industry’s biggest environmental liabilities. Its sought-after chips have triggered a new wave of water- and chemical-intensive factories, drained power grids from inside massive data centers, and set the stage for a looming e-waste problem.
Jensen Huang was reckless with the environment, too
Nvidia’s environmental footprint extends way beyond its own offices.
Under Huang’s leadership, Nvidia clashed with environmental groups seeking to hold the company accountable for its so-called “hidden” emissions. Huang has talked up the idea of using AI to fight climate change while his company’s supply chain emissions ballooned. Nvidia’s investments, meanwhile, have supported the buildout of data centers that have sparked intense backlash for both their local and global impact. Now, after the CEO’s shocking resignation amid a sprawling sex-and-espionage scandal, advocates are urging Nvidia to turn the page.
He compared AI to a surgeon who has “to cut you open to save you.”
“Jensen Huang has failed to put climate responsibility at the heart of the company’s growth strategy, to slow down the unchecked expansion of data centres or to prevent its chips from being deployed in unethical applications like automated warfare,” Avex Li, Greenpeace East Asia’s project lead for AI supply chain campaign, said in a press release Thursday. The organization is now pushing interim CEO Colette Kress to commit Nvidia to decarbonizing by investing in renewable energy, as well as ensuring its technology is used in a way that “respects human rights.” Nvidia didn’t immediately respond to requests for comment from The Verge.
Huang has projected optimism about how AI can boost the adoption of renewable energy, even as the planet-heating emissions of tech companies — including his own — have grown in the generative AI era. “If you want to turn a corner on climate change, if you want a future that’s sustainable, lean into A.I. It is the best opportunity we have to get there,” Huang said in a September episode of The Ezra Klein Show, arguing that electricity demand for AI is leading companies to buy more sustainable energy.
In the same interview, however, he admitted data centers will rely on more fossil fuels in the near term, and that building up the infrastructure for AI will likely result in “an enormous amount of pain and suffering.” He compared AI to a surgeon who has “to cut you open to save you.”
Nvidia’s supply-chain emissions have grown 725 percent since 2020, according to an analysis of the company’s public disclosures by research analyst Ketan Joshi and several environmental organizations, including Greenpeace and Climate Action Against Disinformation, published in September. It’s an increase of about 9.4 million metric tons of planet-heating pollution, roughly equivalent to the emissions from nearly 25 gas plants over a year. Supply chain emissions the company disclosed for fiscal year 2026 reached around 10.7 million metric tons of CO2, according to Nvidia’s latest sustainability report.
Joshi and his co-authors approximated how much greenhouse gas pollution comes from the use of chips the company sells, a category Nvidia doesn’t include in its sustainability reports. Those emissions could have reached 21 million metric tons in 2025, according to the report, based on estimated chip power consumption. That level of pollution puts Nvidia on par with Russia’s state-owned coal company, according to Joshi.
Those “indirect” emissions — from its supply chain and the use of its products — make up the bulk of Nvidia’s climate impact. The carbon footprint of facilities Nvidia actually owns and operates looks much smaller in comparison because Nvidia designs chips that other companies like TSMC then manufacture. Greenhouse gas emissions coming directly from Nvidia-operated facilities and vehicles only reached 9,822 metric tons in fiscal year 2026, the company’s sustainability report shows. And in 2025, the company reached a goal of matching 100 percent of its facilities’ electricity use with clean energy purchases.
Greenpeace wants Nvidia to extend that goal to its entire manufacturing supply chain. When Greenpeace activists disrupted Huang’s speech at Nvidia GTC in Berlin last month, he responded onstage by saying, “I’ll talk to you guys later … All important issues, but let me get through my keynote.” In the Thursday press release, Greenpeace says Nvidia has yet to meet with Greenpeace despite the organization’s attempts to “seek dialogue” with the company over the past two years.
“One of Huang’s defining legacies is inflating a speculative AI bubble, pouring billions of dollars into infrastructure with little regard for the real-world consequences inflicted on local communities and the climate,” Katrin Wu, Big Tech campaigner at Greenpeace International, said in an email to The Verge. “Huang may be gone, but the ‘tech colonialism’ Nvidia perpetuates continues.”
“Huang may be gone, but the ‘tech colonialism’ Nvidia perpetuates continues.”
Beyond Nvidia’s day-to-day operations, Huang threw his weight around as the CEO of one of the world’s most valuable companies — chumming it up with President Donald Trump and lobbying for the US to allow sales of its powerful chips to China. The company’s influence on the global economy extended beyond chips as it invested in data centers stocking its GPUs.
And with electricity supply often the thorniest bottleneck to building more and bigger data centers, Nvidia’s long tendrils reached into the energy sector as well. NVentures, the company’s venture capital arm, has funded battery recycling company Redwood Materials and startups developing AI tools to optimize power grids and make data centers more responsive to fluctuations in energy demand.
Nvidia joined one of those startups, Emerald AI, along with Google to cofound the AI Energy Management Alliance (AEMA) in September. The alliance advocates for strategies that tech companies promote as ways to keep data centers from overwhelming power grids or raising utility bills for other customers, including generating power on-site and making “flexible” facilities that can pause operations during times of peak energy demand. Notably, some environmental groups argue that those measures might just help data centers come online faster without fully insulating households from the impact that rising electricity demand has on their air quality or utility bills.
Whether Nvidia’s environmental footprint shrinks or expands from here will depend on whoever steps in to fill Huang’s shoes. Over the years, Greenpeace and other environmental groups have pointed out that despite having an outsize impact on the environment, Nvidia doesn’t necessarily come under the same public scrutiny as more consumer-facing brands like Apple or Google. Huang’s exploits have thrust the company into a new kind of spotlight, however, just as data centers increasingly face backlash from nearby communities. Nvidia won’t be able to hide from the glare.

libc/string/wcwidth.c
/*
 * This is an implementation of wcwidth() (defined in
 * IEEE Std 1002.1-2001) for Unicode.
 *
 * http://www.opengroup.org/onlinepubs/007904975/functions/wcwidth.html
 *
 * In fixed-width output devices, Latin characters all occupy a single
 * "cell" position of equal width, whereas ideographic CJK characters
 * occupy two such cells. Interoperability between terminal-line
 * applications and (teletype-style) character terminals using the
 * UTF-8 encoding requires agreement on which character should advance
 * the cursor by how many cell positions. No established formal
 * standards exist at present on which Unicode character shall occupy
 * how many cell positions on character terminals. These routines are
 * a first attempt of defining such behavior based on simple rules
 * applied to data provided by the Unicode Consortium.
 *
 * For some graphical characters, the Unicode standard explicitly
 * defines a character-cell width via the definition of the East Asian
 * FullWidth (F), Wide (W), Half-width (H), and Narrow (Na) classes.
 * In all these cases, there is no ambiguity about which width a
 * terminal shall use. For characters in the East Asian Ambiguous (A)
 * class, the width choice depends purely on a preference of backward
 * compatibility with either historic CJK or Western practice.
 * Choosing single-width for these characters is easy to justify as
 * the appropriate long-term solution, as the CJK practice of
 * displaying these characters as double-width comes from historic
 * implementation simplicity (8-bit encoded characters were displayed
 * single-width and 16-bit ones double-width, even for Greek,
 * Cyrillic, etc.) and not any typographic considerations.
 *
 * Much less clear is the choice of width for the Not East Asian
 * (Neutral) class. Existing practice does not dictate a width for any
 * of these characters. It would nevertheless make sense
 * typographically to allocate two character cells to characters such
 * as for instance EM SPACE or VOLUME INTEGRAL, which cannot be
 * represented adequately with a single-width glyph. The following
 * routines at present merely assign a single-cell width to all
 * neutral characters, in the interest of simplicity. This is not
 * entirely satisfactory and should be reconsidered before
 * establishing a formal standard in this area. At the moment, the
 * decision which Not East Asian (Neutral) characters should be
 * represented by double-width glyphs cannot yet be answered by
 * applying a simple rule from the Unicode database content. Setting
 * up a proper standard for the behavior of UTF-8 character terminals
 * will require a careful analysis not only of each Unicode character,
 * but also of each presentation form, something the author of these
 * routines has avoided to do so far.
 *
 * http://www.unicode.org/unicode/reports/tr11/
 *
 * Markus Kuhn -- 2007-05-26 (Unicode 5.0)
 *
 * Permission to use, copy, modify, and distribute this software
 * for any purpose and without fee is hereby granted. The author
 * disclaims all warranties with regard to this software.
 *
 * Latest version: http://www.cl.cam.ac.uk/~mgk25/ucs/wcwidth.c
 */

===== THIRD_PARTY.md =====
# Third-party notices
Project-owned public APP sources: [GPLv3 with the FM1 SDK linking exception](LICENSE.md). Component licenses also apply to firmware and web builds that include those components.
| Component | Source / license |
| --- | --- |
| 303 | [Open303](https://github.com/RobinSchmidt/Open303/tree/313bf0d9ade7c1dcb6b3a74f5ea1780a29d70074), MIT; C adaptation with FM1 drive and MIDI handling. |
| 808 / Pluck | [DaisySP](https://github.com/daisyaudio/DaisySP/tree/2c72eaf9eac5fc0dca1919d65d606da907832618), MIT; selected Plaits drum and String models with FM1 voices and controls. |
| SVF | [stmlib](https://github.com/pichenettes/stmlib/tree/d18def816c51d1da0c108236928b2bbd25c17481), MIT; fixed-rate filter adaptation. |
| FM model | [MSFA](https://github.com/google/music-synthesizer-for-android/tree/f67d41d313b7dc85f6fb99e79e515cc9d208cfff) / [Dexed msfa](https://github.com/asb2m10/dexed/tree/eebb748b70c5a1338afa3945e8b1ea783c9c02fe/source/msfa), Apache-2.0; C adaptation of algorithms, envelopes, LFO and note scaling, with FM1 arithmetic and controls. |
| PSG | [emu2149](https://github.com/digital-sound-antiques/emu2149/tree/441f3dc295a9b82db16921461f0678b483db8304), MIT; memory/table adaptation and ultrasonic output fix. |
| SEA codec | [SEA](https://github.com/Daninet/sea-codec), MIT; fixed-format encoder, decoder and tables. |
| Packager | [jl-misctools](https://github.com/kagaimiq/jl-misctools/tree/0a5b12db0ef38f3042acffbe2452730a37fd2405), MIT; format/codec adaptation with FM1 validation and layout. |
| Native C runtime | `sdk/lib/libc.a`, Newlib-derived routines; native runtime notices below. |
| Native compiler runtime | `sdk/lib/libcompiler_rt.a`; identified compiler-rt routines, legacy MIT / University of Illinois-NCSA notices below.  |
| micro-ecc | Identified routines in `sdk/lib/libfm1_engine.a`; BSD-2-Clause notice below. |
| JieLi SDK material | Identified AC79 SDK material retains its upstream terms; see SDK notices below. |
| APP / open web engine tuning | Incorporates contributions by [Vikram Rojo (PR #2)](https://github.com/m-vave/fm1_open/pull/2), with FM1 integration changes (2026-10-17). Original file licenses and notices are retained. |
| Configuration resource | `sdk/tools/pack/cfg_tool.bin`, identical to the file in the identified official JieLi Apache-2.0 SDK distribution; see below. |
| Boot/update resources and recovery firmware | `sdk/tools/pack/uboot.boot`, `ota.bin`, `boot-config.bin`, and `sdk/firmware/FM-1_015.fwsc`, Apache-2.0; see the resource terms below. |
| Original 128-voice DX7 bank | `app/fm_factory.inc`: extracted without parameter or ordering changes from the bundled M-VAVE V15 recovery image (Apache-2.0), losslessly encoded for Flash in 2026. Reproduce with `node tools/Generate-Factory-DX7.mjs`; the tool pins the source package and decoded VMEM SHA-256 hashes. Demo project recipes remain separate. |

/*
 * This is an implementation of wcwidth() (defined in
 * IEEE Std 1002.1-2001) for Unicode.
 *
 * http://www.opengroup.org/onlinepubs/007904975/functions/wcwidth.html
 *
 * In fixed-width output devices, Latin characters all occupy a single
 * "cell" position of equal width, whereas ideographic CJK characters
 * occupy two such cells. Interoperability between terminal-line
 * applications and (teletype-style) character terminals using the
 * UTF-8 encoding requires agreement on which character should advance
 * the cursor by how many cell positions. No established formal
 * standards exist at present on which Unicode character shall occupy
 * how many cell positions on character terminals. These routines are
 * a first attempt of defining such behavior based on simple rules
 * applied to data provided by the Unicode Consortium.
 *
 * For some graphical characters, the Unicode standard explicitly
 * defines a character-cell width via the definition of the East Asian
 * FullWidth (F), Wide (W), Half-width (H), and Narrow (Na) classes.
 * In all these cases, there is no ambiguity about which width a
 * terminal shall use. For characters in the East Asian Ambiguous (A)
 * class, the width choice depends purely on a preference of backward
 * compatibility with either historic CJK or Western practice.
 * Choosing single-width for these characters is easy to justify as
 * the appropriate long-term solution, as the CJK practice of
 * displaying these characters as double-width comes from historic
 * implementation simplicity (8-bit encoded characters were displayed
 * single-width and 16-bit ones double-width, even for Greek,
 * Cyrillic, etc.) and not any typographic considerations.
 *
 * Much less clear is the choice of width for the Not East Asian
 * (Neutral) class. Existing practice does not dictate a width for any
 * of these characters. It would nevertheless make sense
 * typographically to allocate two character cells to characters such
 * as for instance EM SPACE or VOLUME INTEGRAL, which cannot be
 * represented adequately with a single-width glyph. The following
 * routines at present merely assign a single-cell width to all
 * neutral characters, in the interest of simplicity. This is not
 * entirely satisfactory and should be reconsidered before
 * establishing a formal standard in this area. At the moment, the
 * decision which Not East Asian (Neutral) characters should be
 * represented by double-width glyphs cannot yet be answered by
 * applying a simple rule from the Unicode database content. Setting
 * up a proper standard for the behavior of UTF-8 character terminals
 * will require a careful analysis not only of each Unicode character,
 * but also of each presentation form, something the author of these
 * routines has avoided to do so far.
 *
 * http://www.unicode.org/unicode/reports/tr11/
 *
 * Markus Kuhn -- 2007-05-26 (Unicode 5.0)
 *
 * Permission to use, copy, modify, and distribute this software
 * for any purpose and without fee is hereby granted. The author
 * disclaims all warranties with regard to this software.
 *
 * Latest version: http://www.cl.cam.ac.uk/~mgk25/ucs/wcwidth.c
 */
